conviction_note: The baseline's 1.75% median comes from monthly 6-Ks and is flagged unusable; the structurally important fact is that Zegna already published its second-quarter revenue on 2026-07-23, so this release adds only the profit-and-loss below the revenue line, which caps the surprise - and I tilt negative because the stock fell 17.4% over the twenty sessions into it with nothing in the capture to explain the move.

findings.finding: Second-quarter revenue was already released on 2026-07-23 (a 6-K, recorded in the corpus as a 'Q2 26 Earnings Results & Recap' with a -0.5% reaction), so the 2026-09-03 release - two 6-Ks the same morning - carries the half-year profit-and-loss, margins and any outlook rather than the top line; the revenue surprise, which is what usually moves a luxury name, is already in the price.
findings.corpus_ref: filings.json 6-K entries dated 2026-07-23 and two dated 2026-09-03; docs/43f565083d963dd453a2e5a3a2e636882ad642e2.txt entry dated 2026-07-23T11:59:21Z
findings.why_not_priced: The split-release structure (revenue in July, full accounts in September) is standard for European issuers and is exactly why the baseline's small median reactions look the way they do - but it is also why the run-in matters more than the print. The unpriced element is the composition: with revenue known, the entire surprise sits in gross margin and operating leverage at a wholesale-exposed luxury group, and there is no news search for this ticker (n_queries=0 in every admissible sweep) and no consensus anywhere in the capture to anchor a margin expectation.
findings.independence: none - this rests on the filing cadence and one Stocktwits line from the same document.

findings.finding: The stock fell 17.4% over twenty sessions and 8.5% over the last five into the print, on 848,200 shares a day, with no filing after a 6-K on 2026-08-24 and a passive 13G/A on 2026-08-12, no insider activity since 2026-05-11, and an admissible social stream containing exactly one message in the six weeks before the event.
findings.corpus_ref: baseline tape (run_up_5d -8.52%, run_up_20d -17.42%); filings.json shows nothing between 2026-08-24 and the print
findings.why_not_priced: A 17% de-rating with no company disclosure, no insider action and effectively zero observed commentary is an unexplained move, and unexplained moves into a print are more often information than noise. The honest alternative is that it is a sector de-rating - the same run also shows lululemon falling and a broader consumer-discretionary drawdown - in which case it carries no company-specific content, and that is why I keep this small.
findings.independence: The LULU capture in this same run records a coincident luxury and premium-apparel de-rating from a different set of sources, which supports the sector rather than the company reading - see the LULU hunt file's 'Lululemon cuts 2026 forecast as sales slump across Americas' item.

baseline_tension: It cuts against the tagged reaction history (6 of 8 up) but that history is monthly-6-K noise the baseline itself rejects, and it sits with the run-in, which is sharply negative.
corpus_limits: No option chain, so no implied move or skew. No news search was run for this ticker; the admissible corpus is one document body containing one message, which makes this among the thinnest captures in the sample and is why neither finding is large. The baseline's reaction history is explicitly cadence_implausible (14-day inferred cadence, last 'print' ten days earlier) and I did not use it as a base rate.
